outcome: successful vaginal birth after cesarean section (VBAC)
cohort: 400 pregnant women with a previous cesarean section, divided into groups based on short (<18 months) or longer (>=18 months) inter-pregnancy intervals.
finding: Increasing inter-pregnancy interval is associated with increased chances of successful VBAC and fewer reported complications.
mod_finding: Previous vaginal delivery and spontaneous onset of labor significantly increased VBAC success, while augmentation of labor increased the rate of cesarean section.
